findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — Concurrent member-page requests can resolve out of order and overwrite the latest page with stale members.
app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — The existing group-members endpoint now returns an object instead of the previously serialized array without a versioned route or compatibility response.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — The public members endpoint now defaults every group to 50 users while its template has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members silently lose members from the page.
app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — totalPages adds one after floor division, producing an extra empty page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — Member reloads preserve an offset that can become out of range after deleting the last member on a page, leaving the admin on an empty page instead of returning to the last valid page.
app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint accepts an uncapped limit, allowing one request to load and serialize an entire large group.
app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Adding members performs an individual user lookup for every unbounded comma-separated username, creating linear database work for a single request.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — The automatic-group removal test invokes the action with PUT although the new member-removal route accepts DELETE, so it does not verify the routed endpoint.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — The new paginated members response and its changed JSON shape have no request coverage for pagination bounds or metadata, leaving the public membership contract unverified.
app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:6 — The new client-side pagination flow has no tests for an exact-full page or empty group, so its page-boundary behavior is unverified.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — The existing group-members endpoint now returns an object instead of the previously serialized array without a versioned route or compatibility response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the members endpoint in groups_controller.rb changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` which returns a serialized array, to `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: {...} }` which returns an object with 'members' and 'meta' keys. This is a breaking API change - any existing client code expecting an array will now receive an object instead. The finding correctly identifies this as a backwards-incompatible change without versioning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — The public members endpoint now defaults every group to 50 users while its template has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members silently lose members from the page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the members endpoint in groups_controller.rb now defaults to limit=50 with pagination (lines 22-35). Looking at the public group members template (group/members.hbs), it only changes from 'model' to 'members' in the each loop but adds no pagination controls. The admin template has pagination controls (previous/next buttons), but the public group/members.hbs template does not. This means groups with more than 50 members will only show the first 50 without any way to see the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint accepts an uncapped limit, allowing one request to load and serialize an entire large group.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb lines 22-23 that `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any user-provided limit value without an upper bound cap. While there's a default of 50, a malicious user could pass limit=999999 to load and serialize an entire large group in one request, causing performance/DoS issues. This is a security/performance bug as there's no maximum limit enforced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Adding members performs an individual user lookup for every unbounded comma-separated username, creating linear database work for a single request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the add_members action at line 71 splits usernames by comma and performs a User.find_by_username lookup for each one in a loop. This is visible in the diff: `usernames.split(",").each do |username| if user = User.find_by_username(username)`. While this is a valid performance concern (N+1 queries pattern), it's not a bug - the code functions correctly. It's an architectural/performance concern that a reasonable reviewer might flag, especially since there's no limit on the number of usernames that can be passed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — The new paginated members response and its changed JSON shape have no request coverage for pagination bounds or metadata, leaving the public membership contract unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the members endpoint in groups_controller.rb was changed from returning a simple array to returning a paginated response with metadata (total, limit, offset). Looking at the spec file changes, there are no new tests added for the groups_controller.rb members endpoint - the spec changes are only for admin/groups_controller_spec.rb. The finding correctly identifies that the new pagination behavior and JSON structure for the public /groups/:group_id/members endpoint lacks test coverage. This is a legitimate concern about missing tests for changed functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:6 — The new client-side pagination flow has no tests for an exact-full page or empty group, so its page-boundary behavior is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new pagination logic in admin-group.js.es6 with currentPage and totalPages computed properties that use division and floor operations. The spec file (admin/groups_controller_spec.rb) is updated but contains no tests for the client-side pagination behavior, particularly edge cases like empty groups (user_count == 0) or when offset equals user_count exactly. The finding correctly identifies that the new pagination flow lacks test coverage for boundary conditions. This is a legitimate concern about missing tests for newly added nontrivial logic.
